K01-pos1.label: violation
K01-pos1.note: Rehearsals service imports the ProductionOpened class from the productions domain/events folder instead of the public contract.

K01-pos2.label: violation
K01-pos2.note: New casting lookup imports the productions repository interface from the productions domain folder to read a title.

K01-twin1.label: clean
K01-twin1.note: Rehearsals service imports the event type from the productions index (public API) instead of the contract file.

K01-twin2.label: clean
K01-twin2.note: Casting lookup reaches productions only through its index and its contracts folder.

K01-legit.label: clean
K01-legit.note: Api helper in rehearsals imports the context own domain file and shared-kernel only; deep imports inside one context are fine.

K02-pos1.label: violation
K02-pos1.note: Production aggregate imports the Logger of a web framework package and logs inside close().

K02-pos2.label: violation
K02-pos2.note: Actor aggregate imports and instantiates an infrastructure calendar adapter to answer availability.

K02-twin1.label: clean
K02-twin1.note: Actor answers availability through a policy interface declared in the domain; no infrastructure import.

K02-twin2.label: clean
K02-twin2.note: Actor gains a rate using the shared-kernel Money value object; the domain imports only shared-kernel.

K02-legit.label: clean
K02-legit.note: Infrastructure adapter depends on an application port and a domain repository interface, which is the allowed direction.

K03-pos1.label: violation
K03-pos1.note: confirm() saves the booking and also the actor instance after starting an engagement.

K03-pos2.label: violation
K03-pos2.note: New moveBooking command loads two rooms and saves both in one command.

K03-twin1.label: clean
K03-twin1.note: Engagement is started by a separate single-aggregate command that reacts to the confirmed event; confirm() saves only the booking.

K03-twin2.label: clean
K03-twin2.note: moveBooking works on one room: release and book, then a single save.

K03-legit.label: clean
K03-legit.note: confirm() loads the actor to check it exists but saves only the booking.

K04-pos1.label: violation
K04-pos1.note: Repository gains saveWithActor, which persists a booking and an actor aggregate in one call; confirm() uses it.

K04-pos2.label: violation
K04-pos2.note: Room repository gains saveBoth, persisting two room aggregates in one call (no caller yet).

K04-twin1.label: clean
K04-twin1.note: Repository saveWithSlots stores one room together with its own inner slot entities.

K04-twin2.label: clean
K04-twin2.note: Repository gains a read-only findByProduction query; nothing is persisted.

K04-legit.label: clean
K04-legit.note: save() also appends a history snapshot row (not an aggregate) next to the booking.

K05-pos1.label: violation
K05-pos1.note: confirm() calls ProductionService.addCast of the productions context synchronously instead of publishing the event.

K05-pos2.label: violation
K05-pos2.note: close() calls RehearsalService.release of the rehearsals context synchronously through a helper.

K05-twin1.label: clean
K05-twin1.note: Closing a production publishes a ProductionClosed event; rehearsals reacts in its own handler wired through the bus.

K05-twin2.label: clean
K05-twin2.note: Casting reads the production through its public service to refuse offers on a closed production; it writes only its own aggregate.

K05-legit.label: clean
K05-legit.note: ProductionService gets an own handler that writes only its own aggregate when a booking is confirmed; the bus invokes it.

K06-pos1.label: violation
K06-pos1.note: Composition root defines a BookingDesk facade that confirms a booking in casting and adds the cast in productions.

K06-pos2.label: violation
K06-pos2.note: Composition root defines an openAndReserve function that writes a production and a rehearsal room directly through both repositories.

K06-twin1.label: clean
K06-twin1.note: Composition root builds a read-only snapshot helper that only queries two contexts through their services.

K06-twin2.label: clean
K06-twin2.note: Composition root wraps a single-context command (open a production) and records it; no second aggregate is written.

K06-legit.label: clean
K06-legit.note: Composition root subscribes an extra audit handler that only records booking ids; wiring through the bus is the composition root job.

K07-pos1.label: violation
K07-pos1.note: open() announces to the external ticketing system inside the unit-of-work callback.

K07-pos2.label: violation
K07-pos2.note: offer() checks the external calendar inside the unit-of-work callback, through a local callback and an early throw.

K07-twin1.label: clean
K07-twin1.note: open() commits first and calls the ticketing system after the transaction, translating failures.

K07-twin2.label: clean
K07-twin2.note: offer() checks the calendar in a private helper before the transaction starts.

K07-legit.label: clean
K07-legit.note: Inside the transaction offer() only touches local repositories (reads the actor, saves the booking); the remote check stays before it.

K08-pos1.label: violation
K08-pos1.note: The rule that a production needs a show to open is decided in ProductionService.open; the aggregate no longer checks it.

K08-pos2.label: violation
K08-pos2.note: The rule that a slot ends after it starts is decided in the controller; RehearsalRoom.book no longer checks it.

K08-twin1.label: clean
K08-twin1.note: Service only wraps the aggregate error with context; the aggregate still decides whether a production can open.

K08-twin2.label: clean
K08-twin2.note: Controller validates that start and end are numbers (request shape); the ordering rule stays in the aggregate.

K08-legit.label: clean
K08-legit.note: Controller authorises the caller role before opening; authorisation is an application concern, not an aggregate rule.

K09-pos1.label: violation
K09-pos1.note: decline() checks the offered status in the service and the aggregate checks it again.

K09-pos2.label: violation
K09-pos2.note: bookSlot checks start<end through a local flag and RehearsalRoom.book checks it again.

K09-twin1.label: clean
K09-twin1.note: The aggregate exposes canDecline() and uses it itself; the service only reads it for a query.

K09-twin2.label: clean
K09-twin2.note: Controller turns thrown aggregate errors into a result object; it makes no check of its own.

K09-legit.label: clean
K09-legit.note: Controller trims the title input (normalisation) and the aggregate setter still validates it; no rule is duplicated.

K10-pos1.label: violation
K10-pos1.note: The cast capacity (set invariant owned by Production) is checked in ProductionService.addCast; the aggregate no longer checks it.

K10-pos2.label: violation
K10-pos2.note: The cast capacity is checked in the controller from the DTO (maxCast exposed); the aggregate does not check it.

K10-twin1.label: clean
K10-twin1.note: Aggregate exposes openSlots (derived from maxCast and cast) and the DTO reports it; the capacity check stays in Production.addCast.

K10-twin2.label: clean
K10-twin2.note: Aggregate gains addCastMany that reuses addCast, so capacity is enforced inside; the service only forwards the ids.

K10-legit.label: clean
K10-legit.note: Production gains replaceCast, which swaps one actor for another inside the aggregate and keeps the size within maxCast.

K11-pos1.label: violation
K11-pos1.note: bookSlot uses an in-process Set of busy room ids as a lock instead of relying on the aggregate.

K11-pos2.label: violation
K11-pos2.note: confirm() serialises per booking id with a Map of promises (a mutex chain) held in the service.

K11-twin1.label: clean
K11-twin1.note: The room aggregate carries a version and the repository rejects stale saves (optimistic concurrency), no in-process lock.

K11-twin2.label: clean
K11-twin2.note: The service keeps a Map cache of room names for reads; it is a read cache, not a lock or consistency boundary.

K11-legit.label: clean
K11-legit.note: The calendar adapter (infrastructure) de-duplicates concurrent identical lookups with an in-flight Map; a technical optimisation, not an aggregate lock.

K12-pos1.label: violation
K12-pos1.note: confirm() multiplies fee by weeks in the service and hands the total to booking.recordTotal.

K12-pos2.label: violation
K12-pos2.note: bookSlot sums the booked hours of the room in a service helper and sets them back on the room.

K12-twin1.label: clean
K12-twin1.note: The room computes its own bookedHours() and the DTO reports it; the service performs no calculation.

K12-twin2.label: clean
K12-twin2.note: offerAnnual converts an annual fee from the command input into a weekly fee before creating the booking; no aggregate state is involved.

K12-legit.label: clean
K12-legit.note: payrollFor sums the totals of several bookings for reporting; it reads aggregates (using their own totalDue) and hands nothing back.

K13-pos1.label: violation
K13-pos1.note: The ticketing port returns HttpResponse, a type declared in the infrastructure adapter file.

K13-pos2.label: violation
K13-pos2.note: The availability port takes a Transaction parameter, leaking a transaction type into the port signature.

K13-twin1.label: clean
K13-twin1.note: The ticketing port returns an AnnounceResult type declared in the port file itself.

K13-twin2.label: clean
K13-twin2.note: The availability port gains a quote method using the shared-kernel Money value object and plain parameters.

K13-legit.label: clean
K13-legit.note: The adapter uses an HttpResponse type internally while the port keeps returning void; the vendor-shaped type never reaches the port.

K14-pos1.label: violation
K14-pos1.note: The productions public API re-exports the Production aggregate class.

K14-pos2.label: violation
K14-pos2.note: RoomDto exposes RoomSlot entities in its slots field and the service hands them out directly.

K14-twin1.label: clean
K14-twin1.note: A new ProductionSummaryDto of plain fields is published through contracts and the index; no entity type leaves the context.

K14-twin2.label: clean
K14-twin2.note: A new ActorDto of plain fields is added to casting contracts and mapped in the service.

K14-legit.label: clean
K14-legit.note: CastBookingDto exposes the fee as the shared-kernel Money value object, which is a value object and not an entity.

K15-pos1.label: violation
K15-pos1.note: CastingService constructor is typed against the concrete CalendarAvailabilityAdapter instead of the port.

K15-pos2.label: violation
K15-pos2.note: RehearsalService constructor is typed against InMemoryRehearsalRoomRepository instead of the repository interface.

K15-twin1.label: clean
K15-twin1.note: CastingService takes a narrower slice of the port (Pick of isFree); still typed against the port.

K15-twin2.label: clean
K15-twin2.note: An audit decorator wraps the calendar adapter and is itself typed against the port; the service still receives a port.

K15-legit.label: clean
K15-legit.note: An infrastructure decorator wraps the concrete calendar adapter; concrete types inside infrastructure and the composition root are normal.

K16-pos1.label: violation
K16-pos1.note: CastBooking keeps an Actor aggregate object in a field (assignActor) instead of only the actor id.

K16-pos2.label: violation
K16-pos2.note: Actor keeps a list of CastBooking aggregate objects instead of their ids.

K16-twin1.label: clean
K16-twin1.note: CastBooking records an understudy by actor id only, through a typed setter.

K16-twin2.label: clean
K16-twin2.note: Actor keeps the ids of its bookings, not the booking objects.

K16-legit.label: clean
K16-legit.note: CastBooking holds a list of Money value objects (bonuses); a value object held by value is part of the aggregate, not another aggregate.
